references.text: Earlier in the same chapter it is mentioned that one must not touch the carcass of unclean animals, which reinforces the message about impurity through contact.
Repeats the principle that whoever touches the carcass of an unclean animal becomes unclean until evening and must wash their clothes.
Extends the laws regarding impurity by contact to include small creeping things that are unclean.
Concerns impurity from touching the carcass of clean animals that die naturally, with the impurity lasting until evening.
Mentions purification for those who eat animals that died naturally or were torn apart.
Priests who touch something unclean become unclean until evening and must cleanse themselves.
Detailed laws about impurity from touching dead people, expanding the principle of impurity through contact with the dead.
Repeats the prohibition against touching the carcass of unclean animals in Deuteronomy.
The prophet Haggai asks the priests about the transmission of impurity by touch, confirming the principle from Leviticus.
